main.pausedBody: The camera is off. Nothing is being analysed.
main.pausedIdle: Nobody was in view for {{n}} minutes. The camera was turned off.
main.browserPreview: Browser preview: gestures are recognised, but no keys are sent to PowerPoint and the bar cannot float above the presentation. Use the installed app for that.

prefs.title: Preferences

handHint.left: Only your left hand changes slides. Gesture freely with your right.
handHint.right: Only your right hand changes slides. Gesture freely with your left.
handHint.either: Both hands can swipe. Per gesture, only the hand that clearly swipes first counts.

sensHint.low: Good if you gesture a lot while talking.
sensHint.high: Good for small movements or standing far from the camera.

prefs.presentersHint: Who may change slides when several people are in view?

speakerHint.manual: To take over, raise an open hand for about 1 second.
speakerHint.auto: Magic Hand detects who is speaking. An open hand overrides it at any time.

autoSignalHint.mouth: Whoever is speaking (mouth movement) may change slides.
autoSignalHint.movement: Whoever moves the most may change slides.
autoSignalHint.both: Combines speaking and movement, most reliable.

resolutionHint.1280x720: For large rooms, needs more power.

keysHint.arrows: Works in PowerPoint, Keynote, Google Slides and PDF viewers.

prefs.pauseShortcutHint: Works even while the presentation is in front.
prefs.privacyHint: Camera images are processed in memory only, never stored and never sent. Only your preferences and calibration are saved.
prefs.deleted: Deleted. No data is stored anymore.
prefs.farAssistHint: When you stand far away, Magic Hand searches for your hand near your wrist and, if needed, uses your arm movement.
prefs.soundHint: A short, quiet tone so you know it worked without looking.
prefs.autoPause: Turn the camera off when nobody is there
prefs.autoPauseHint: Saves battery and protects privacy when you leave the room.

pillCameraHint.off: Only the slim bar floats above the presentation.
pillCameraHint.large: A large camera view with your tracked hand floats above the presentation. Drag to move it.

dev.title: Developer
dev.hint: For testing only. Show/hide with Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + D.
dev.dryRunHint: Recognise gestures but do not send keys.
dev.delegateHint: Applied the next time detection starts.
dev.detectHint: Threshold frame captured until key sent
dev.reactionHint: Start of the movement until key sent (includes the gesture itself, target < 500 ms)
dev.recordPrivacy: Only hand points (coordinates) are recorded, never images. Only with the consent of everyone in view.
dev.noPersons: No people tracked (the pose model runs every few frames).

help.title: Help
help.step1: Hold one hand still in front of the camera for about a second. The ring fills up, then gestures are active. No slide changes before that.
help.step2: Click “Present” or into your presentation so the keys arrive there.
help.step3Next: Swipe briskly to the {{dir}}: next slide.
help.step3Return: Then simply bring your hand back. That does not trigger anything.
help.tip1: Slow or diagonal movements while explaining are ignored.
help.tip3: Press {{shortcut}} to pause at any time, even during the presentation.

trouble.noSlide: The presentation must be in front: click into it once. On macOS, Magic Hand needs the Accessibility permission. Also check that dry run is off in the developer settings.
trouble.camera: Allow camera access in System Settings. Close other apps using the camera (Teams, Zoom). On Windows: Settings → Privacy → Camera → “Let desktop apps access your camera”.
trouble.tooOften: Set sensitivity to “Calm” or choose a preferred hand. The other hand can then gesture freely.
trouble.notRecognized: Swipe faster and further, about two to three hand lengths. Make sure there is light from the front and stay in view. At a large distance, the “High” resolution helps.
trouble.slow: Set the resolution to “Low”. Close demanding programs.
trouble.permission: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Camera and Accessibility: enable Magic Hand. Then restart the app.

privacyBody: All camera images are processed on this device only. They stay in memory and are discarded immediately.
No images, videos or hand data are stored or transmitted. Magic Hand makes no internet connection.
Only your preferences and calibration (e.g. the area where you present) are saved. You can delete them in Preferences at any time.
The camera is only on while gesture control runs. It is off while paused.
Only the calibrated area is analysed, not the audience.
help.aboutBody: Magic Hand is a project in the Natural User Interfaces module at ZHAW.

try.title: Try it
try.lead: Swipe briskly to the {{dir}} or back. No key is sent.
try.armFirst: First hold a hand still for about a second until the ring is full.

toast.ignored_not_speaker: Person {{n}} is not the speaker. Raise an open hand for 1 s to take over.
toast.speaker: Person {{n}} now changes the slides

welcome.title: Welcome to Magic Hand
welcome.lead: Change slides with a swipe, without walking back to your laptop.
welcome.p1: Swipe briskly: next or previous slide.
welcome.p2: Hold your hand still for a moment: gestures become active. Nothing happens before that.
welcome.privacy: Everything stays on this device. No images are stored or sent.

direction.title: Which direction feels natural?
direction.lead: Try both directions in front of the camera and pick which one means “next slide”.
direction.note: You can change this later in Preferences.

framing.title: Are you in the picture?
framing.lead: Stand where you will present. The outline shows roughly where to stand.
framing.lightLow: Too dark: light from the front helps.
framing.lightHigh: Too bright or backlit: do not stand in front of a window.
framing.tooFar: A bit far away. Come closer or choose the “High” resolution.
framing.tooClose: Too close: take a step back.
framing.handSmall: Your hand is very small in the picture.
framing.showHand: Hold a hand up to the camera.

zone.title: Your presenting area
zone.observing: Stay where you present for a moment. Magic Hand is proposing an area …
zone.fullFrameNote: Only now is the whole picture looked at, to find you.
zone.lead: Gestures are only recognised inside this area. The audience outside is not analysed.
zone.nobody: Nobody was in view. You can set the area by hand or use the whole picture.
zone.tipDrag: Drag the frame or its handles. Arrow keys move it, with Shift they resize it.

arm.title: Hold your hand still
arm.lead: Hold one hand still in front of the camera for about a second until the ring is full.
arm.why: This tells Magic Hand you are ready. No slide ever changes before that.

practice.title: Practice round
practice.lead: Swipe {{n}}× in each direction, the way you would while presenting. Magic Hand learns your speed and reach.
practice.note: No keys are sent during practice.

summary.title: Tuned to you
summary.notEnough: Not enough practice swipes were recognised to tune anything. The current values stay.

done.title: All set
done.lead: Click “Present”: Magic Hand turns into a small bar and hands the focus back to your presentation.
done.calibrateLater: Use “Calibrate” later to tune Magic Hand more closely to your movements.

hints.noHand: Hold a hand up to the camera and keep it still for a moment to start.
hints.focus: The key went to Magic Hand itself. Click into your presentation or on “Present”.
hints.present: Tip: “Present” shrinks Magic Hand into a bar above your presentation.
hints.takeover: Several people in view: to take over, raise an open hand for about a second.
hints.far: You are far away: swipe with big, clear arm movements.

study.intro: Test session: Magic Hand asks for swipes in alternating directions, then measures false triggers while you talk freely. No keys are sent.
study.promptNext: Now: swipe to the next slide
study.promptPrev: Now: swipe to the previous slide
study.freeTalk: Talk freely and gesture as usual. Do not swipe.
